Fig. 6. (a) Feature significance based on the Shapley value, and (b) the impact of different features on the multilayer perceptron (MLP) predictions*. * The dot plot visualizes individual SHAP values for each data instance concerning the given features. Each dot represents the SHAP value of an instance for that feature. The color spectrum from red to blue signifies the feature value, with red being high and blue being low. A value of zero implies no impact on the prediction of the model. Positive SHAP values push the output higher, and negative values push the output lower.

Fig. 7. Decision-making process* of the transmembrane pressure (TMP) pre­ diction using multilayer perceptron (MLP). * The black vertical line at the center of the decision figure represents the fundamental value of the model, defined as the mean TMP value. Each line shows the predictive behavior of the test dataset, and the left-to-right move­ ment of the line indicates whether each feature increases or decreases the output value relative to the mean value. Beginning at the bottom of the figure, the prediction line demonstrates how the MLP model accumulates from the basic TMP average to the ultimate output value at the top of the figure.
